mainTopic: Honoring תלמידי חכמים and honoring שבת: how the חכמים prepared for שבת, the rewards for honoring it, and making the שבת meal special
overview: This amud opens with the end of אביי's statement about celebrating when a scholar finishes a מסכתא. Then רבא and מר בר רב אשי describe how they treat a צורבא מרבנן in court. The גמרא returns to כבוד שבת: רבי חנינא and רבי ינאי greet שבת as a queen and a bride, and great אמוראים buy fine food and do preparation work with their own hands, the way one would serve a great guest. The story of יוסף מוקר שבי and the pearl teaches that whoever spends for שבת, שבת repays him. רבי asks why the wealthy merit their riches: in ארץ ישראל because they tithe, in בבל because they honor the תורה, and everywhere else because they honor שבת, as the butcher of Laodicea shows. רבי יהושע בן חנניה tells the קיסר that the 'spice' of שבת works only for those who keep it. The amud ends with how to honor יום הכפורים and the שבת meal, and with רב ששת making sure his lecture did not cut into עונג שבת. A story about רבי זירא begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי makes a celebration for the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The last words of אביי's statement: when a scholar finishes a מסכתא, he makes a feast for the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: I make a festive day for the Sages.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a sentence that began on the previous amud. אביי said that when he saw a young scholar finish a מסכתא, he would make a celebration for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is proud of honoring Torah learning by celebrating a סיום. This sets the theme for the next lines, where other אמוראים say how they honored תלמידי חכמים.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement. It is the end of אביי's sentence ("תיתי לי... דשלים מסכתיה") on the previous amud.

phrases.english: I make a festive day for the Sages.
phrases.notes: End of אביי's statement, which began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's statement from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי celebrates a scholar's completion of a מסכתא with a feast for the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא searches for a scholar's merits in judgment
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he deserves reward because he does not go to sleep until he has searched for every merit of a צורבא מרבנן who comes before him in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: May I be rewarded, because when a young scholar comes before me for judgment, I do not lay my head on the pillow until I have searched for his merits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds his own way of honoring Torah scholars. When one comes to his court, he works hard to find arguments in the scholar's favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אביי, רבא uses the phrase "תיתי לי" (may I be rewarded) for something he does to honor תלמידי חכמים. His honor shows up in the courtroom: he works hard to find זכות for a scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: may [reward] come to me, I deserve credit
I turn over / search for his merits

phrases.english: Rava said: May I receive reward,
because when a young Torah scholar comes
before me for judgment,
I do not rest my head on the pillow
until I have searched for his merits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel "תיתי לי" statement about honoring scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא searches hard for a scholar's merits before ruling on his case.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי disqualifies himself from judging a scholar
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי says he cannot judge a scholar at all, because a scholar is as dear to him as himself, and no one can see guilt in himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: I am disqualified from judging a young scholar. Why? Because he is as beloved to me as my own self, and a person cannot see fault in himself.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי goes further than רבא. He says he cannot judge a scholar at all, and he explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא leaned toward the scholar but still judged him. מר בר רב אשי says his love for scholars makes him biased, like a relative. So he steps aside completely, based on the rule that no one can find himself guilty.

keyTerms.meaning: a person does not see guilt in himself

steps.whatToRemember: Honoring scholars in court can mean searching for their merits (רבא) or stepping aside because of bias (מר בר רב אשי).

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
I am disqualified from judging a young Torah scholar.
What is the reason?
Because he is as beloved to me as my own self,
and a person does not find fault in himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי פְּסִילְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבא's approach a step further: total self-disqualification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge who loves scholars like himself is biased and should not judge them.

steps.title: רבי חנינא goes out to greet the שבת Queen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to כבוד שבת. רבי חנינא would wrap himself and stand at sunset on ערב שבת, saying: "Come, let us go out to greet שבת the queen."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא would wrap himself in his garment and stand at sunset on ערב שבת, and say: Come, let us go out to greet שבת the queen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, honoring שבת, and starts a list of how great Sages did it. רבי חנינא treated שבת's arrival like a royal visit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrapping himself in his garment and going out shows he saw שבת as a queen to be welcomed. The honor is in how he got ready and went toward שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the turning of the day on ערב שבת (sunset)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the קבלת שבת custom, and for the words "לכו ונצא" and "בואי כלה" in לכה דודי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina would wrap himself and stand
at sunset on Shabbat eve, and say:
"Come and let us go out to greet Shabbat the queen."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of honoring scholars and returns to the main theme of כבוד שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Welcome שבת as a queen by dressing up and going out to greet her.

steps.title: רבי ינאי welcomes שבת as a bride
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי would put on fine clothes and say: "Enter, O bride! Enter, O bride!"
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי would put on fine garments and cover himself, and say: Come, O bride! Come, O bride!
steps.whatsHappening: A second example of greeting שבת. רבי ינאי dressed up and welcomed שבת like a bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא pictured a queen; רבי ינאי pictures a bride. A bride brings joy and closeness, so this image adds love and happiness to the honor.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai would put on fine garments and cover himself,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, שבת, but the corrected wording drops it and puts ומיכסי ('and covered himself') in its place.

phrases.english: and say: "Enter, O bride! Enter, O bride!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel example of greeting שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Welcome שבת joyfully, like a bride, wearing fine clothes.

steps.title: The biscuits were for שבת, not for the guest
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא visited רבה בר רב נחמן and was served many fine biscuits. He asked if they had known he was coming. They answered: Are you more important to us than שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא visited the house of רבה בר רב נחמן. They served him three סאה of oiled biscuits. He said: Did you know I was coming? They said: Are you more important to us than her (שבת)?
steps.whatsHappening: A story showing how much food was prepared in honor of שבת. The guest thought it was for him, but it was really for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large amount of food made the guest think he was being honored. The family's answer shows that שבת is a more important guest than even a great Sage.

keyTerms.meaning: are you more important to us than her (שבת)?

steps.confusionAlert: "מינה" (than her) refers to שבת, even though שבת is not named in the line.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna happened to come
to the house of Rabba bar Rav Nachman.
They brought before him three se'a of oiled biscuits.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: מִי הֲוָה יָדְעִיתוּן דְּאָתֵינָא?
phrases.english: He said to them: Did you know that I was coming?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מִי עֲדִיפַתְּ לַן מִינַּהּ?
phrases.english: They said to him: Are you more important to us than her (Shabbat)?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַבָּה בַּר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from greeting שבת to preparing food in its honor.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine food is prepared for שבת because שבת is the most honored guest.

steps.title: רבי אבא buys meat from thirteen butchers
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא bought meat from thirteen different butchers for שבת, set it at the door, and urged the cooks to hurry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא bought meat for thirteen plain staters from thirteen butchers. He would hand it over at the door hinge and say to them: Hurry and prepare it, hurry and prepare it!
steps.whatsHappening: Another example of preparing for שבת. רבי אבא spent money on many kinds of meat and hurried to get them cooked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying from thirteen butchers got him the best variety. Rushing it in at the door and urging speed shows how eager he was to honor שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bought for thirteen
plain staters' worth of meat
from thirteen butchers,
and he would hand them over at the door hinge,
and say to them: "Hurry and prepare it, hurry and prepare it!"

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא זָבֵן בִּתְלֵיסַר אִסְתִּירֵי פְּשִׁיטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of food preparation for שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spending money and effort on fine food honors שבת.

steps.title: רבי אבהו fans the fire himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, a wealthy and important man, sat on an ivory chair and fanned the cooking fire for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו would sit on an ivory chair and fan the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The list now turns to Sages who did שבת preparation work with their own hands. Even רבי אבהו, who sat on an ivory chair, fanned the fire himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ivory chair shows how important and wealthy he was. Even so, he did a simple kitchen job himself to take part in honoring שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu would sit
on an ivory chair and fan the fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה יָתֵיב אַתַּכְתָּקָא דְשִׁינָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from buying food to doing the work personally.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a great person should personally help prepare for שבת.

steps.title: רב ענן wears a work garment for שבת preparation
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן put on a simple black garment while preparing for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן would put on a simple black garment.
steps.whatsHappening: Another Sage who worked for שבת himself. רב ענן changed into simple work clothes for the job, and the next line gives the source for doing this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not cook in his fine clothes. He saved those for שבת itself and wore a plain garment for the messy work.

phrases.english: Rav Anan would put on a simple black garment,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another Sage doing hands-on preparation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wear simple clothes for שבת preparation work.

steps.title: Source: different clothes for different tasks
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן's practice is supported by a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל: clothes worn while cooking for one's master should not be worn while pouring his wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The clothes in which a servant cooked a pot for his master, he should not wear when he pours a cup of wine for his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for רב ענן's practice. Each task should be done in suitable clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dirty cooking clothes are not fitting for serving the master at the table. In the same way, רב ענן cooked in work clothes and kept his fine clothes for honoring שבת itself.

keyTerms.meaning: as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught (a ברייתא)
pour / mix a cup of wine

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the idea of having special clothing for שבת, separate from weekday and work clothes.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Garments in which one cooked a pot for his master —
he should not pour a cup for his master in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רב ענן's practice.
steps.raayaObject: רב ענן's practice of wearing a plain garment for שבת preparation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל about separate clothes for cooking and serving.

steps.title: A list of Sages who prepared for שבת with their own hands
steps.stepSummary: Many אמוראים each did a different preparation job for שבת: roasting, salting fish, lighting lamps, twisting wicks, cutting beets, chopping wood, and preparing kindling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא roasted the head of an animal. רבא salted a שיבוטא fish. רב הונא lit lamps. רב פפא twisted wicks. רב חסדא cut beets. רבה and רב יוסף chopped wood. רבי זירא prepared thin kindling sticks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists many great Sages and the hands-on job each one did to prepare for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jobs are simple and physical, yet the leaders of the generation did them themselves. The point is that preparing for שבת in person is a מצוה, not something only to hand off to others.
steps.whyThisMatters: Halacha follows this: a person should personally do something to prepare for שבת, even if he is very important (as the רמב"ם and שולחן ערוך rule).

phrases.english: Rav Safra would roast the head.
Rava salted a shibuta fish.
Rav Huna lit lamps.
Rav Pappa twisted wicks.
Rav Chisda cut beets.
Rabba and Rav Yosef chopped wood.
Rabbi Zeira prepared thin kindling sticks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the list of Sages who did hands-on work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great Sages personally did simple jobs to prepare for שבת.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק carries things in and out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק carried items in and out on his shoulder. He reasoned: if רבי אמי and רבי אסי visited me, wouldn't I carry for them? So surely I should for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק would load things on his shoulder and go in, load and go out. He said: If רבי אמי and רבי אסי came to visit me, would I not carry things before them?
steps.whatsHappening: Another Sage working for שבת, but this time he explains his reasoning. He compares שבת to hosting great Sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic: for important guests, a person does the serving himself. שבת is at least as honored a guest, so he serves it the same way. This explains the whole list: personal work shows personal honor.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak
would load on his shoulder and enter, load on his shoulder and exit.
He said: If there happened to visit me
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
would I not carry on my shoulder before them?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מְכַתֵּף וְעָיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the list with a stated reason for doing personal work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Serve שבת personally, just as you would personally serve great visiting Sages.

steps.title: Another version: רבי אמי and רבי אסי did the carrying
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רבי אמי and רבי אסי were the ones who carried, reasoning: if רבי יוחנן visited us, wouldn't we carry before him?
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: רבי אמי and רבי אסי would load on their shoulders and go in, load and go out. They said: If רבי יוחנן came to visit us, would we not carry before him?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of who said this. Here רבי אמי and רבי אסי carry, and they compare שבת to a visit from their teacher רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea stays the same; only the people change. In this version, the comparison is to רבי יוחנן, the teacher of רבי אמי and רבי אסי.
steps.whatToRemember: Honoring שבת means greeting it (queen/bride), preparing fine food, and doing preparation work yourself, the way you would serve a great guest.
steps.confusionAlert: "איכא דאמרי" here does not argue with the idea. It only changes who did the carrying and whom they compared שבת to.

phrases.english: And some say:
Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
would load on their shoulders and enter, load on their shoulders and exit,

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: אִילּוּ אִיקְּלַע לַן רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: they said: If Rabbi Yochanan happened to visit us,
would we not carry on our shoulders before him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי מְכַתְּפִי וְעָיְילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate version of step 12, with different people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same principle: serve שבת personally, as you would serve your great teacher.

steps.title: The story of יוסף מוקר שבי, who honored שבת
steps.stepSummary: A rich גוי is told that יוסף מוקר שבי will end up with all his property. He tries to escape this by turning everything into one pearl. The pearl is lost and swallowed by a fish, and the fish is sold to יוסף for שבת. יוסף finds the pearl inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man called יוסף מוקר שבי (יוסף who honors שבת). A very rich גוי lived near him. Astrologers told the גוי that יוסף would end up eating all his property. So he sold everything and bought one pearl, which he put in his hat. While he was crossing a river on a ferry, the wind blew the hat into the water, and a fish swallowed it. The fish was caught and brought in late on Friday afternoon (ערב שבת). The fishermen asked, 'Who buys at a time like this?' People told them, 'Take it to יוסף מוקר שבי. He always buys.' They brought it to him, and he bought it. He cut it open and found the pearl. He sold the pearl for thirteen containers full of gold coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its theme of honoring שבת by telling a story. A man who always spent money on שבת receives a great fortune.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי tries to fight what the כלדאי predicted by turning all his wealth into one small pearl he could keep on his body. That plan backfires: the pearl ends up inside the very fish that יוסף buys for שבת. יוסף was known for buying for שבת even at the last minute, when no one else would buy, and this habit is exactly what brings the wealth to him.

keyTerms.meaning: יוסף who honors שבת (a nickname earned from his habit)
Close to nightfall on ערב שבת (late Friday afternoon)

phrases.english: Yosef who honors Shabbat:
there was a certain non-Jew in his neighborhood
whose property was very plentiful.
The astrologers said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ נִכְסֵי — יוֹסֵף מוֹקַר שַׁבֵּי אָכֵיל לְהוּ.
phrases.english: All of the property, Yosef who honors Shabbat will consume it.
He went and sold all of the property,
bought a pearl with it, and placed it in his hat.
While he was crossing on a ferry,
the wind blew it off and threw it into the water,
and a fish swallowed it.
They pulled it up and brought it close to nightfall on Shabbat eve.
They said: Who buys at a time like this?
They said to them: Go bring it

phrases.aramaic: לְגַבֵּי יוֹסֵף מוֹקַר שַׁבֵּי דִּרְגִיל דְּזָבֵין.
phrases.english: to Yosef who honors Shabbat, who regularly buys.
They brought it to him, and he bought it.
He tore it open and found the pearl inside it.
He sold it for thirteen containers of golden dinars.
phrases.notes: Following תוספות, עיליתא means vessels or containers full of coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹסֵף מוֹקַר שַׁבֵּי, הֲוָה הָהוּא גּוֹי בְּשִׁבָבוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of personal effort for שבת with a story about the reward for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who spends on honoring שבת is repaid, even in surprising ways.

steps.title: The old man's lesson: שבת repays its lenders
steps.stepSummary: An old man meets יוסף and states the moral of the story: whoever lends to שבת, שבת pays him back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain old man met him and said: Whoever lends to שבת, שבת repays him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story closes with a short saying that sums up its lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money spent on שבת is pictured as a loan, not a loss, and שבת itself pays the loan back. The pearl is that repayment.

keyTerms.meaning: An old man (often understood as a wise or heavenly figure)

steps.whatToRemember: מאן דיזיף שבתא פרעיה שבתא: spending for שבת is a loan that שבת pays back.

phrases.english: A certain old man met him and said:
Whoever lends to Shabbat, Shabbat repays him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the moral of the story in step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שבת repays those who spend money in its honor.

steps.title: רבי asks why the wealthy of ארץ ישראל merit wealth
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי what merit earns the rich people of ארץ ישראל their wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי asked רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי: The rich people in ארץ ישראל, through what do they merit their wealth?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins with a question. This sets up a series of questions and answers about why the wealthy deserve their wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that wealth is a reward for some good deed. It asks which deed explains the wealth of people in ארץ ישראל in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question or inquiry)
Through what do they merit (deserve) it?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rebbi asked Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשִׁירִים שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמָּה הֵן זוֹכִין?
phrases.english: The wealthy of Eretz Yisrael, through what do they merit?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related discussion about what earns people wealth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The merit behind the wealth of the rich in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Answer: because they tithe
steps.stepSummary: The rich of ארץ ישראל become wealthy because they give מעשרות, based on a דרשה of the words עשר תעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because they tithe, as the פסוק says, 'You shall surely tithe (עשר תעשר).' This means: tithe so that you will become rich.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי answers that the wealthy of ארץ ישראל are rewarded for separating מעשרות, and he brings a פסוק to support this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word עשר תעשר is read as a wordplay: עשר (tithe) sounds like עשר (wealth). Since the מצוה of מעשר applies to produce grown in ארץ ישראל, it fits the wealthy there.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because they tithe,
as it says: 'Tithe, you shall tithe':
tithe so that you will become rich.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are rewarded for tithing, based on the דרשה עשר בשביל שתתעשר.

steps.title: What about the wealthy of בבל?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks what merit earns wealth for the rich in בבל, where the מצוה of מעשר does not fully apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rich people in בבל, through what do they merit their wealth?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי follows up with the same question about the wealthy in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer about tithing does not fully explain בבל, because the מצוה of מעשרות applies mainly to produce of ארץ ישראל. So a different merit is needed there.

phrases.english: Those in Babylonia, through what do they merit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question to a place the first answer does not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The merit behind the wealth of the rich in בבל.

steps.title: Answer: because they honor the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The rich of בבל are rewarded because they honor the תורה and its scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because they honor the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the wealthy of בבל honor the תורה, and that merit brings them wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל was full of תלמידי חכמים, so the wealthy there could earn merit by honoring and supporting תורה scholars.

keyTerms.meaning: They honor the תורה (and those who study it)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: He said to him: Because they honor the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18.

steps.title: What about the wealthy of other lands?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks about the wealthy in other countries, where there is neither מעשר nor many תורה scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those in other lands, through what do they merit their wealth?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks the third and last question, about the wealthy everywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither earlier answer covers places without מעשרות and without many תורה scholars. A merit that applies everywhere is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Other lands (outside ארץ ישראל and בבל)

phrases.english: And those in other lands, through what do they merit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question again, to places neither earlier answer covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The merit behind the wealth of the rich in other lands.

steps.title: Answer: because they honor שבת
steps.stepSummary: The rich in other lands are rewarded for honoring שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because they honor שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The final answer brings the discussion back to the main theme: honoring שבת brings wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת can be kept anywhere, so honoring it is a merit available to every Jew in every land. This ties the discussion back to the earlier steps about honoring שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer connects the question-and-answer series to the larger topic of כבוד שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: He said to him: Because they honor Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא's story of the wealthy butcher in Laodicea
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא tells of staying with a very rich host in Laodicea. The host said he became wealthy because, as a butcher, he always set aside the finest animal for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא בר אבא said: Once I was a guest of a homeowner in Laodicea. They brought before him a gold table that took sixteen men to carry. Sixteen silver chains were attached to it, and bowls, cups, pitchers, and flasks were attached to it. On it were all kinds of food, delicacies, and spices. When they set it down, they said: 'The earth and all that fills it belongs to God.' When they took it away, they said: 'The heavens are God's, but the earth He gave to people.' I asked him: My son, how did you merit this? He told me: I was a butcher, and whenever I had a fine animal, I said, 'This one will be for שבת.' I said to him: Fortunate are you that you merited this, and blessed is God who gave you this merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to prove the last answer: a wealthy man outside ארץ ישראל earned his riches by honoring שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man was not a scholar and lived far from ארץ ישראל, yet he became very rich because he always saved the best meat for שבת. The two פסוקים his household said show that he knew his wealth came from הקב"ה: the first when the table was set, and the second when it was cleared.

keyTerms.meaning: Laodicea, a city in Asia Minor

steps.whatToRemember: Wealth in ארץ ישראל comes from מעשר, in בבל from honoring the תורה, and everywhere else from honoring שבת, as shown by the butcher of Laodicea.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:

phrases.aramaic: פַּעַם אַחַת נִתְאָרַחְתִּי אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת בְּלוּדְקִיָּא,
phrases.english: Once I was a guest at a homeowner's house in Laodicea,
and they brought before him a table of gold
that was a load for sixteen people,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שַׁלְשְׁלָאוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף קְבוּעוֹת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: with sixteen silver chains attached to it,

phrases.aramaic: וּקְעָרוֹת וְכוֹסוֹת וְקִיתוֹנִיּוֹת וּצְלוֹחִיּוֹת קְבוּעוֹת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: and bowls, cups, pitchers, and flasks attached to it,
and on it all kinds of food
and all kinds of delicacies and spices.
When they set it down, they would say:
'The earth and all that fills it is God's,' and so on.
And when they removed it, they would say:
'The heavens are God's heavens,
but the earth He gave to mankind.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: בְּנִי בַּמֶּה זָכִיתָ לְכָךְ?
phrases.english: I said to him: My son, how did you merit this?
He said to me: I was a butcher,
and of every animal that was fine,
I said: This will be for Shabbat.
I said to him: Fortunate are you that you merited,
and blessed is God who gave you the merit for this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the answer in step 21 with a real-life example.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the wealthy in other lands merit wealth by honoring שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר אבא's account of the butcher of Laodicea.

steps.title: The קיסר asks why שבת food smells so good
steps.stepSummary: The קיסר asks רבי יהושע בן חנניה why cooked שבת food has such a strong, pleasant smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: The קיסר said to רבי יהושע בן חנניה: Why does the smell of a שבת dish spread so strongly?
steps.whatsHappening: A new short story begins with a question from the קיסר. This sets up רבי יהושע's answer about the special quality of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קיסר noticed something special about שבת food and wants to know the natural reason for it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא:
phrases.english: The Emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה תַּבְשִׁיל שֶׁל שַׁבָּת רֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף?
phrases.english: Why does the cooked dish of Shabbat give off such a fragrance?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens another story about the special quality of שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the special smell of שבת food.

steps.title: Answer: a spice called שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that the Jews have a spice named שבת that they put into the food, and it makes the smell spread.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We have a certain spice, and its name is שבת. We put it into the dish, and its smell spreads.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers playfully that the secret ingredient is 'שבת' itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'spice' is a parable: the holiness of שבת is what gives the food its special taste and smell. Some explain this as a wordplay on a real spice called שבת (dill).
steps.confusionAlert: There is no real secret seasoning here. The 'spice' is שבת itself, meaning its holiness, which is why the next step says it only works for those who keep שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: תַּבְלִין אֶחָד יֵשׁ לָנוּ וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: He said to him: We have a certain spice, and its name is Shabbat,
which we put into it, and its fragrance spreads.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: תַּבְלִין אֶחָד יֵשׁ לָנוּ וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קיסר's question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A 'spice' called שבת gives the food its smell.

steps.title: The קיסר asks for some of the spice
steps.stepSummary: The קיסר, taking the answer at face value, asks to be given some of this spice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Give us some of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The קיסר asks for some of the spice. This sets up רבי יהושע's punchline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קיסר understands the 'spice' as a physical ingredient that could be handed over. This misunderstanding sets up the point that שבת cannot be separated from keeping it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Give us some of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up request based on the answer in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the קיסר can obtain the spice.

steps.title: The spice works only for those who keep שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains that the 'spice' works only for someone who keeps שבת, and does nothing for someone who does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For anyone who keeps שבת, it works. For someone who does not keep שבת, it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with the lesson: the blessing of שבת comes only to those who keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the 'spice' was שבת's holiness all along, which cannot be bought or handed over. It closes this passage's theme that honoring and keeping שבת brings real, even physical, blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: It helps or works for him

steps.whatToRemember: The special blessing of שבת, whether wealth or the taste of the food, comes only to those who honor and keep it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל הַמְשַׁמֵּר אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת — מוֹעִיל לוֹ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Anyone who keeps Shabbat, it works for him,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּר אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת — אֵינוֹ מוֹעִיל לוֹ.
phrases.english: and one who does not keep Shabbat, it does not work for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל הַמְשַׁמֵּר אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request in step 25 and closes the story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'spice' of שבת is its holiness, which benefits only those who keep שבת.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא asks about 'וְלִקְדוֹשׁ ה׳ מְכוּבָּד'
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא asks רב המנונא to explain the words 'וְלִקְדוֹשׁ ה׳ מְכוּבָּד' in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא said to רב המנונא: What does the verse 'the holy one of ה׳ is honored' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new short discussion. The ריש גלותא asks רב המנונא what the phrase 'the holy one of ה׳ is honored' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ישעיה is mainly about שבת ('call שבת a delight'). However, it also mentions a separate 'holy one of ה׳' that is honored. The question is which holy day this extra phrase is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the official leader of the Jews in בבל
What is the meaning of what is written
The holy one of ה׳ is honored (ישעיה נח:יג)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא:
phrases.english: The Exilarch said to Rav Hamnuna:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The holy one of God is honored"?
phrases.notes: ישעיה נח:יג, the same verse that speaks about calling שבת a delight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories about honoring שבת to a question about a related verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which holy day the phrase 'the holy one of ה׳ is honored' refers to, and how that day is honored.

steps.title: It means יום הכפורים, honored with clean clothing
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא answers that it is יום הכפורים. Since there is no eating or drinking on that day, the תורה says to honor it with clean clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: This is יום הכפורים. It has no eating and no drinking, so the תורה said: honor it with clean clothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא explains that the 'holy one' is יום הכפורים, and that it is honored through clean clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is mostly honored with special food. On יום הכפורים, food is not allowed, so the honor has to be shown another way. Clean, fresh clothing takes the place of the special meals.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for wearing clean, nice clothes on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: He said to him: That is Yom Kippur,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ לֹא אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּה,
phrases.english: when there is no eating and no drinking,
so the Torah said: Honor it with a clean garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the ריש גלותא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse refers to יום הכפורים. Because it has no food, it is honored with clean clothing.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: eat the שבת meal earlier or later
steps.stepSummary: On the word 'וְכִבַּדְתּוֹ' (and you shall honor it, said about שבת), רב says to eat the שבת meal earlier, and שמואל says to eat it later.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall honor it': רב said this means making the meal earlier, and שמואל said it means making it later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about how the timing of the שבת meal honors שבת. רב says earlier, and שמואל says later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that changing the meal time honors שבת. Eating early shows that you are eager for the שבת meal. Eating later builds up your appetite, so you enjoy the meal more.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall honor it (שבת, in ישעיה נח:יג)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different phrase from the 'holy one of ה׳' in the step before. 'וכבדתו' refers to שבת, not to יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: "And you shall honor it": Rav said: To make the meal earlier,
phrases.notes: An early meal shows eagerness for the שבת meal.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: To make it later.
phrases.notes: A later meal means a bigger appetite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same verse, but turns to a different word that is about שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: honor שבת by eating the meal earlier. שמואל: honor it by eating later.

steps.title: How can wealthy people make שבת food different?
steps.stepSummary: The sons of רב פפא בר אבא ask רב פפא how they can make שבת special, since they already eat meat and wine every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רב פפא בר אבא said to רב פפא: People like us, who have meat and wine every day, how can we make שבת different?
steps.whatsHappening: Rich students ask a practical question. If special food is already normal for them every day, how can their שבת meal stand out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the special menu is what makes שבת feel different. For people who eat fine food every day, the menu alone does not change anything. They need another way to mark the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we change it (make it different)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא בַּר אַבָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba said to Rav Pappa:
People like us, for whom there is commonly found
meat and wine every day,
in what way can we change it on Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea of making שבת meals different to people whose daily food is already special.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How people who eat meat and wine every day can make שבת feel different.

steps.title: Change your usual meal time
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers: if you usually eat early, eat later on שבת. If you usually eat late, eat earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If you usually eat early, make it later. If you usually eat late, make it earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells them to honor שבת by changing the time of the meal from their usual schedule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer uses both sides of the רב and שמואל מחלוקת. What matters is making שבת different from the weekday. So the change should go against whatever your normal habit is.
steps.whatToRemember: Honoring שבת means making it stand out from the weekday. If the food is not different, change the timing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי רְגִילִיתוּ לְאַקְדּוֹמֵי — אַחֲרוּהּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: If you are used to eating early, make it later;
if you are used to eating late, make it earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the sons' question, using the earlier/later idea from רב and שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Change the meal time from your weekday habit, earlier or later, so that שבת stands out.

steps.title: רב ששת seated his students so they would leave quickly
steps.stepSummary: In summer, רב ששת seated the students in the sun, and in winter in the shade, so they would get up quickly after the שבת lecture and go enjoy שבת. This passage ends with the name רבי זירא, which begins the next story.
steps.simpleTranslation: In summer, רב ששת would seat the רבנן where the sun reached. In winter, he would seat them where the shade reached, so that they would get up quickly. Then the next story begins: רבי זירא...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how רב ששת made sure his long שבת lecture would not take away from שבת enjoyment. The last words, 'רבי זירא', are setting up the next story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the sun in summer or in the shade in winter is uncomfortable, so the students would not linger after the lecture. They would go home and enjoy their שבת meal. This is a real-life example of how seriously the אמוראים took עונג שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת was not being harsh. The discomfort was on purpose, so the students would go home to their שבת meal.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, in the summer,
would seat the Sages
where the sun would reach.
In the winter, he would seat the Sages
where the shade would reach,
so that they would get up quickly.
Rabbi Zeira
phrases.notes: This opens the next story, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּקַיְטָא מוֹתֵיב לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another practical example of protecting שבת enjoyment, this time through how a שבת lecture was run.
steps.raayaObject: That שבת enjoyment, including the meal, is important enough to shape even how a תורה lecture is run.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב ששת, who seated his students in uncomfortable spots so they would leave promptly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת arranged his students' seating so that the שבת lecture would end promptly and not take away from עונג שבת.
